Fig. 8: Pooled out-of-fold confusion matrices across agreement thresholds (σ ∈ {3, 4, 5}, figure rows) and problem types (P− 2 , P+ 2 , P3, and P5, figure columns). Row-normalized. Errors in the 5-class remain adjacent labels, consistent with granularity failure rather than polarity inversion.

TABLE VI: Agreement metrics (point estimate from 60% annotation resample per image, 95% CI via image bootstrap, N=1,000): nimg = images passing σ filter; nann = annotations per evaluation (nimg × 716, based on 60% of ≈1,194 annotations per image). Cohen’s κ is weighted to account for ordinal distances between classes: unweighted for binary tasks (P2, all errors penalised equally); linear-weighted for P3 (penalty proportional to class distance on the 3-point scale); quadraticweighted for P5 (penalty proportional to the square of the ordinal distance, so confusing Negative with Positive costs far more than adjacent errors). †: σ=5 scores of 1.000 arise from extreme filtering (few images, absent intermediate classes); interpret with caution.
